item.summary: fix: gateway stop throws when port is busy without identified owner (#126085) * fix: gateway stop throws when port is busy without identified owner When `openclaw gateway stop` cannot find the owning process via lsof or the lock file, probe the port using gateway-configured bind hosts (resolveGatewayServiceProbeHosts) before reporting success. If the port is provably busy on a configured interface, throw with actionable guidance (`openclaw gateway status --deep`) instead of silently returning. Uses gateway-scoped probe hosts to avoid false positives from unrelated listeners on different interfaces (e.g. another process on 127.0.0.2 does not trigger an error when the gateway binds 127.0.0.1). Co-authored-by: Cursor * fix: thread selected service context into gateway stop port probe The port probe in stopGatewayWithoutServiceManager passed an empty object to resolveGatewayServiceProbeHosts, causing it to read the caller's process.env instead of the selected service's command environment. A gateway running under a different profile or state directory was probed against the wrong bind configuration. Inline the probe logic from the deleted lifecycle-port-probe.t
